description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Those Self-Governance Tribes described in 503(a) of the Act [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-2(a)] participating in the Title III Tribal Self-Governance Demonstration Project and up to 50 additional Indian Tribes per year that meet the criteria in § 137.18 may participate in self-governance.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.16 — What if more than 50 Indian Tribes apply to participate in self-governance?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The first Indian Tribes who apply and are determined to be eligible shall have the option to participate in self-governance. Any Indian Tribe denied participation due to the limitation in number of Indian Tribes that may take part is entitled to participate in.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.17 — May more than one Indian Tribe participate in the same compact and/or funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, Indian Tribes may either: (a) Each sign the same compact and/or funding agreement, provided that each one meets the criteria to participate in self-governance and accepts legal responsibility for all financial and administrative decisions made under the compact or funding agreement, or.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.18 — What criteria must an Indian Tribe satisfy to be eligible to participate in self-governance?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). To be eligible to participate in self-governance, an Indian Tribe must have: (a) Successfully completed the planning phase described in § 137.20; (b) Requested participation in self-governance by resolution or other official action by the governing body of each Indian Tribe to be.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.20 — What is required during the planning phase?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The planning phase must be conducted to the satisfaction of the Indian Tribe and must include: (a) legal and budgetary research; and (b) internal Tribal government planning and organizational preparation relating to the administration of health programs.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.21 — How does an Indian Tribe demonstrate financial stability and financial management capacity?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The Indian Tribe provides evidence that, for the three years prior to participation in self-governance, the Indian Tribe has had no uncorrected significant and material audit exceptions in the required annual audit of the Indian Tribe's self-determination contracts or self-governance funding agreements with.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.22 — May the Secretary consider uncorrected significant and material audit exceptions identified regarding centralized financial and administrative functions?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, if the Indian Tribe chooses to centralize its self-determination or self-governance financial and administrative functions with non-self-determination or non-self-governance financial and administrative functions, such as personnel, payroll, property management, etc., the Secretary may consider uncorrected significant and material audit exceptions related to.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.23 — For purposes of determining eligibility for participation in self-governance, may the Secretary consider any other information regarding the Indian Tribe's financial stability and financial management capacity?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). No, meeting the criteria set forth in §§ 137.21 and 137.22, shall be conclusive evidence of the required stability and capability to participate in self-governance.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.24 — Are there grants available to assist the Indian Tribe to meet the requirements to participate in self-governance?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, any Indian Tribe may apply, as provided in § 137.25, for a grant to assist it to: (a) Plan to participate in self-governance; and (b) Negotiate the terms of the compact and funding agreement between the Indian Tribe and Secretary.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.25 — Are planning and negotiation grants available?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Subject to the availability of funds, IHS will annually publish a notice of the number of planning and negotiation grants available, an explanation of the application process for such grants, and the criteria for award. Questions may be directed to the Office of.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.26 — Must an Indian Tribe receive a planning or negotiation grant to be eligible to participate in self-governance?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). No, an Indian Tribe may use other resources to meet the planning requirement and to negotiate.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.30 — What is a self-governance compact?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A self-governance compact is a legally binding and mutually enforceable written agreement that affirms the government-to-government relationship between a Self-Governance Tribe and the United States.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.31 — What is included in a compact?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A compact shall include general terms setting forth the government-to-government relationship consistent with the Federal Government's trust responsibility and statutory and treaty obligations to Indian Tribes and such other terms as the parties intend to control from year to year.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.32 — Is a compact required to participate in self-governance?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, Tribes must have a compact in order to participate in self-governance.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.33 — May an Indian Tribe negotiate a funding agreement at the same time it is negotiating a compact?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, at an Indian Tribe's option, a funding agreement may be negotiated prior to or at the same time as the negotiation of a compact.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.34 — May a funding agreement be executed without negotiating a compact?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). No, a compact is a separate document from a funding agreement, and the compact must be executed before or at the same time as a funding agreement.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.35 — What is the term of a self-governance compact?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Upon approval and execution of a self-governance compact, the compact remains in effect for so long as permitted by Federal law or until terminated by mutual written agreement or retrocession or reassumption of all PSFAs.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.40 — What is a funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A funding agreement is a legally binding and mutually enforceable written agreement that identifies the PSFAs that the Self-Governance Tribe will carry out, the funds being transferred from service unit, area and headquarters levels in support of those PSFAs and such other terms.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.41 — What PSFAs must be included in a funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). At the Self-Governance Tribe's option, all PSFAs identified in and in accordance with section 505(b) of the Act must be included in a funding agreement, subject to section 507(c) of the Act [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-6(c)].

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.42 — What Tribal shares may be included in a funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). All Tribal shares identified in sections 505(b)(1) [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-4(b)(1)] and 508(c) of the Act [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-7(c)] may be included in a funding agreement, including Tribal shares of IHS discretionary grants.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.43 — May a Tribe negotiate and leave funds with IHS for retained services?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, at the discretion of the Self-Governance Tribe, Tribal shares may be left, in whole or in part, with IHS for certain PSFAs. These shares are referred to as a “retained Tribal shares.”.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.45 — What terms must be included in a funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A funding agreement must include terms required under section 505(d) of the Act [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-4(d)] and provisions regarding mandatory reporting and reassumption pursuant to section 507(a) of the Act [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-6(a)], unless those provisions have been included in a compact.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.46 — May additional terms be included in a funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, at the Self-Governance Tribe's option, additional terms may be included as set forth in sections 506 [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-5] and 516(b) of the Act [25 U.S.C. 458aaa-15(b)]. In addition, any other terms to which the Self-Governance Tribe and the Secretary agree may.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.48 — What is the effect of incorporating a Title I provision into a compact or funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The incorporated Title I provision shall have the same force and effect as if it were set out in full in Title V.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.49 — What if a Self-Governance Tribe requests such incorporation at the negotiation stage of a compact or funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In that event, such incorporation shall be deemed effective immediately and shall control the negotiation and resulting compact and funding agreement.

title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.55 — What is the term of a funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Yes, the provisions of a funding agreement, including all recurring increases received and continuing eligibility for other increases, remain in full force and effect until a subsequent funding agreement is executed. title: 42 C.F.R. § 137.57 — How is a funding agreement amended during the effective period of the funding agreement?
creator: Public Health Service, Department Of Health And Human Services
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 42 (Public Health), Part 137 (Tribal Self-Governance). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A funding agreement may be amended by the parties as provided for in the funding agreement, Title V, or this part.
